answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independently verified fraud claims succeed. Splitting one attacker’s funds across a thousand identities does not create more backing: each account must tie up capital, and detected Sybils lose it. The umber ledger records each bond, cedar nodes audit claims, and the tide of delayed withdrawals prevents attackers from escaping before review.
